minutes.headline: Committee voted to hire Rich Matthew as director of finance and operations, pending contract; requested $300,000 free cash for special ed reserve.
minutes.summary: The School Committee publicly interviewed a finance director candidate and voted unanimously to hire him pending contract negotiations. It also approved FY27 line item transfers, surplus literacy materials, a 0.5 OT position change, the paraprofessional contract, and a request for special education reserve funding. Discussion covered MCAS and DIBELS results, Brooks House, and track and field turf costs.

public_comment.topic: Chair of PAXAL (special education parent group) announced meetings first Wednesday of each month at 6 PM, alternating official meetings and support groups.

votes.motion: Hire Mr. Matthew as director of finance and operations, pending contract negotiations
Declare non-compliant literacy materials and damaged textbooks surplus and authorize disposal
Accept the report on spring 2026 MCAS and fall DIBELS data
Change the previously voted position to a 0.5 position
State that the school department has no need for the Brooks House
Maintain the high school driveway as is; not allow Brooks House buyer to use it
Update 2026-27 school calendar with new parent teacher conference dates
Accept the fall 2026 athletics participation report
Request $300,000 in free cash for the special education reserve fund if certified at November town meeting
Accept new terms of the paraprofessional contract
Enter executive session and then adjourn

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted unanimously to hire a director of finance and operations, pending contract negotiations, after a public interview.
The Committee voted unanimously to request free cash for the special education reserve fund, if certified at the November town meeting.
The Committee voted unanimously to accept new terms of the paraprofessional contract.
Members voted unanimously to accept FY27 line item transfers and to change a previously voted position to a 0.5 position.
A member said track and field drainage and wall repairs appear to cost about a million dollars before turf; no vote was taken.

why_it_matters: The free cash request rides on the November town meeting warrant article, so residents at that meeting will be asked to certify the money that funds the special education reserve.
The new finance director and the new paraprofessional contract terms shape who prepares the school budget and what a staffing line costs in coming budgets.
Track and field costs have no resolution yet, so a capital request may reach residents later.
watch_next: The November town meeting, where free cash for the special education reserve is to be certified.
The next School Committee meeting, where facilities staff are to present steps and a timeline for the track and field project.
